A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProgressLM and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. The material supports reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and some replaced examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original Progress-Bench evaluations, SFT/RL results, diagnostic analyses, and Human Bench experiments in Tables 1–3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and Human Bench results and adds a 7B training experiment and a manual trajectory-quality assessment.

M1.justification: Episodic retrieval followed by mental simulation, the four-field output format, supervised training, GRPO, and reward weights remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the reward descriptions add documentation; the appendix prompt templates are unchanged and do not establish a revised procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Progress-Bench's 3,325 observations, ProgressLM-45K, and Human Bench's 587 samples across 129 task goals. Modalities, viewpoints, answerability conditions, and robotic embodiments remain the same. The 7B experiment and replaced illustrations do not establish expanded task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 removes Intern3.5-VL-8B from Tables 1–2, the Human Bench comparison, and the detection/distribution plots. Other comparators remain. The new 7B experiment reuses direct-prediction and training-free comparison approaches already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Section 5.5 adds evaluation of a trained Qwen2.5-VL-7B model with one RL epoch because of computational constraints. Section 2.1 introduces a manual audit of 100 randomly sampled trajectories. Existing benchmark settings and the detailed 3B training protocol in Appendix B remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a model-scale generalization analysis and an empirical check of trajectory smoothness supporting interpolation-based labels. Figures 15–16 replace the cross-view and text-demo examples. Existing distribution, coupling, viewpoint, and Human Bench analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the image-editing seed of 42 and the same per-sample distribution analyses. Neither reports repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new trajectory audit reports a proportion without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds the 7B results in Table 3 and the finding that 86% of audited trajectories are fully smooth. Intern3.5-VL-8B results disappear, and Figures 15–16 contain replacement case outputs. Text-demo NoThink UDA changes from 74.7% to 72.7% for Qwen2.5-VL-7B and from 68.3% to 65.3% for Intern3.5-VL-38B in Figures 4 and 13. Retained answerable-table and Human Bench scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: v1's explicit interval/boundary sampling domains in Equation 2 and mathematical definition of NSE are omitted in v2, leaving less precise descriptions. The interpolation formula and SFT/GRPO objectives remain equivalent. No theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The rewritten abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: single-observation progress evaluation, the retrieval/simulation paradigm, conditional benefits of training-free prompting, and strong performance from trained ProgressLM-3B. The comparison with GPT-5 and task-disjoint training claims remain.

C2.justification: New Section 8 explicitly limits applicability beyond monotonic manipulation tasks and discusses possible reward, anomaly-detection, and agent applications. Section 5.5 adds a scaling interpretation, although its claim of improvement across metrics conflicts with Table 3's higher false-rejection rates versus direct prediction. Revised case captions also soften assertions about internal world modeling.

D1.justification: v2 newly describes reference and progress rewards as negative relative errors and supplies the new 7B experiment's one-epoch RL budget. Exact sampling and NSE specifications are dropped. Appendix hardware, 3B hyperparameters, training time, prompt templates, and code/model/data links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands the multimodal reasoning literature and adds connections to world models, web agents, and self-improvement. It removes the DepthLM citation and the substantive comparison with concurrent Robo-dopamine, which v1 used to distinguish explicit reasoning from scalar regression. These changes extend beyond bibliographic restyling.

P1.justification: Most main-text sections are extensively rewritten and condensed. Problem formulation is merged into the benchmark overview, headings and captions are shortened, and scalability, limitations, and acknowledgments sections are added. Author affiliation and correspondence information also change; much appendix prose remains intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column presentation, substantially resizing and relocating figures and tables. Figures 5–8 are concentrated on one page, Algorithm 1 and a scaling table are added, and Figures 15–16 are replaced. Other appendix illustrations are retained but rearranged and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful trajectory-quality and 7B evidence, explicit limitations, and a Figure 16 that now matches its cup-stacking discussion. However, it loses exact NSE and sampling definitions, retains the 14-model claim after removing a baseline, and overstates the new scaling results: Table 3 shows worse AFRR than direct prediction in both modalities. These gains and reporting weaknesses leave the net quality change uncertain.
